title: The Death of Seneca
credits: Synthetic rehearsal voices; original procedurally composed ambient score; historical excerpts identified and attributed; all other dialogue is reconstructed. Pompeia Paulina survived, as recorded in Tacitus Annals 15.64.

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Incertum est quo loco te mors exspectet. Itaque tu illam omni loco exspecta.
cues.source: Latin · Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.7 · his earlier writing

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: The soldiers have arrived.

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Then the order has come.

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: You speak as though you have been waiting for them.

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I have been waiting for death. Not for the sound of their footsteps.

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: What happens now?

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: They have given me no choice. But I can choose how to meet it.

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: Then I will share your fate.
cues.source: Reconstructed dialogue, based on Tacitus, Annals 15.63

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I asked you to live.

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: You asked me to live without you.

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Vitae delenimenta monstraveram tibi, tu mortis decus mavis.
cues.source: Latin · words attributed to Seneca by Tacitus, Annals 15.63

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I showed you the consolations of life. You prefer the honour of death.

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: I do not know how to leave you here alone.

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Nor do I know how to leave you.

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: Are you not afraid?

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Accipio condicionem. Non reformido iudicium.
cues.source: Latin · Seneca, Epistulae morales 26.6 · his earlier writing

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: I wrote that before tonight.

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: A sentence is easier to hold than a hand.

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: Let me stay.

cues.speaker: SENECA
cues.text: Remember my life. Not only this room.
cues.source: Reconstructed dialogue inspired by Tacitus, Annals 15.62

cues.speaker: PAULINA
cues.text: Seneca.
